feedback: This is iteration 0, so no earlier race or outcome exists yet. The Integrator had to make three decisions for your geometry. First, the five sensors at ±0.02 m with 12 mm footprints overlap well, so a proportional controller can use a linear lateral-position weighting without dead zones. Second, the 0.03 m forward lead at y = 0.05 m is still a hypothesis, and the controller uses only a light derivative term to damp it. Third, the 0.12 m wheel track gives enough turn authority at kp 2.0 by the contract's 350 PWM per unit turn, but whether this is enough at 1.5 m/s is unknown. Interpret the next race as follows: if line_loss_events are above zero on the s-bend or slalom, the sensor spread is probably too narrow for the bend curvature, so widen the spread (for example ±0.03 m with the same count) before changing the lead. If steering_oscillation is high while line loss is zero, the forward lead is causing overshoot, so reduce the lead to y = 0.03 m before changing the spread. If max_error is low and completion holds but the completion time exceeds 3 s, the wheel track or body is limiting speed, so try a smaller wheel_radius or lower mass.
requested_changes: Test sensor spread at x = ±0.03 m (keep 5 sensors, 0.012 m footprint) if the next race shows any line_loss_events on the s-bend or slalom, because the baseline ±0.02 m spread may not cover sharp bends.
Test forward sensor lead y = 0.03 m (instead of 0.05 m) if steering_oscillation is high on the slalom while line_loss_events remain zero, to reduce overshoot from lead distance.
Test wheel_track 0.10 m (instead of 0.12 m) only if the robot completes but max_error is high on the slalom, to increase yaw response, and keep the other geometry fixed to isolate the effect.
